items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now les
items.summary:
Dusting off this tweet from April because this gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is *widening*. It's now less "two groups of people speaking past each other" and more a sharp funnel.

- Napkin math somewhere around 6B people (~75% of the population) have barely come in contact with LLMs at all.
- Around 1-2B (~20%) are casual and infrequent users of free-tier ChatGPT-like products. This group sees derpy chatbots and treats them a bit like a better Google search, a writing aid, or etc. Maybe an agent tries to book you a flight. I have non-tech friends who (reasonably, imo) say they have not much use for it at all. Even many professionals outside of math&code are in this tier. For example, execs and many other functions spend a lot of their time talking to other people, so while they understand what is happening intellectually, it is still second-hand and a bit abstract.
- Now we get to professional use of frontier-grade LLMs in math&code. Somewhere around 20M people (0.2%) see first-hand that large, complex projects that used to take them weeks/months can now be completed by agents with a prompt. Building apps, copying apps, translating apps, decompiling apps from binaries... This has all happened very quickly and recently - less than 1 year ago, I was writing code manually by hand, typing memorized computer code commands into a code editor character by character, occasionally pressing Tab to autocomplete a little chunk of code.
- And finally we get to the ~5,000 people (~0.00006%) with access to frontier-grade systems internally. The external world has seen the preview. It looks like swarms of thousands of agents collaborating over weeks on software mega projects: minting zero days, running cyber attacks and defenses at machine speeds, discovering new science, advancing the frontier of mathematics. Things that would have taken top professionals in the industry years of work. Meanwhile, human review and comprehension are starting to fall behind. For example, people are still involved in the "archeology" of the OpenAI-HF incident from many months ago. Mathematicians may be poring over the 722 manuscripts on frontier mathematics for a while.

The funnel is driven by a combination of factors:
1. The impact scales with ambition, problem size, and horizon. A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about. This aspect drives the consumer / professional dimension of the funnel.
2. The jaggedness of the system (which I have written about a lot separately). Capability peaks in domains that are digital, verifiable and economically valuable. This is because LLM capability emerges from reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards on a curated environment mixture driven by revenue potential. This aspect primarily drives the area (e.g. math&code) dimension of the funnel.
3. Access. Free-tier, paid-tier, internal.

So this is the weirdness of the moment. The general public has mostly not interacted with these systems. When they have, it looks like a derpy chatbot. The majority of professionals still see only a modest uplift. And a small sliver of professionals are experiencing the vertigo of the curve going vertical. And it is all happening at the same time.

items.title: 最近，不少 Claude 和 ChatGPT 用户反映账号突然被封。Claude 用户频繁遇到身份验证，有人提交中国护照后立即被封。ChatGPT 则从 11 月 7 日前后出现集中封号投诉，免费用户、Plus、每月 200 美元的 Pro
items.summary:
最近，不少 Claude 和 ChatGPT 用户反映账号突然被封。Claude 用户频繁遇到身份验证，有人提交中国护照后立即被封。ChatGPT 则从 11 月 7 日前后出现集中封号投诉，免费用户、Plus、每月 200 美元的 Pro 用户，甚至企业账号都有人中招。

Claude 的身份验证从今年 4 月就已开始推行。用户可能被要求通过第三方平台 Persona 上传护照等证件，再拍摄自拍照核验身份。10 月底以来，不少老用户突然遇到验证要求。有人用中国护照验证后立即被封，也有人顺利通过。一位用户提交护照后被秒封，申诉第二天又恢复了账号。

Anthropic 官方禁止从中国大陆等未支持地区使用 Claude。公司在 9 月的安全报告中明确表示，系统会识别未经授权转售 Claude、账号来自中国等受限制地区的风险信号，并要求相关用户验证身份，验证失败就会封号。

OpenAI 也开始严格限制多账号使用。根据官方最新文件，同一张银行卡关联过多订阅，会导致新账号无法购买会员；同一台设备登录过多付费账号，也会触发限制，甚至出现付费成功却无法使用的情况。限制覆盖 Go、Plus 和各档 Pro 会员。

OpenAI 最近还向符合条件的 Pro 用户赠送与会员价格等额的 API 额度，最高每月 500 美元。这类额度也成为第三方中转站转卖的对象，供其他用户使用。OpenAI 明确禁止转卖 API 额度或共享账号，违规可导致封号。

两家公司近期还相继更新了使用政策。Anthropic 于 10 月 8 日公布新规，进一步明确中国大陆等未支持地区的访问限制，11 月 12 日生效。OpenAI 则于 10 月 21 日公布新规，要求直接提供 GPT 模型访问的中转平台事先获得官方批准，11 月 20 日生效。

items.title: arXiv paper 1706.03762
items.summary:
Provided proper attribution is provided, Google hereby grants permission to

scholarly works.
Attention Is All You Need
Ashish Vaswani∗
Google Brain
avaswani@google.com
Noam Shazeer∗

noam@google.com
Niki Parmar∗
Google Research
nikip@google.com
Jakob Uszkoreit∗
Google Research
usz@google.com
Llion Jones∗
Google Research
llion@google.com
Aidan N. Gomez∗ †
University of Toronto
aidan@cs.toronto.edu
Łukasz Kaiser∗
Google Brain
lukaszkaiser@google.com
Illia Polosukhin∗ ‡
illia.polosukhin@gmail.com
Abstract
The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or
convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best
performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention
mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer,
based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions
entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to
be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly
less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-
to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including
ensembles, by over 2 BLEU. On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task,
our model establishes a new single-model state-of-the-art BLEU score of 41.8 after
training for 3.5 days on eight GPUs, a small fraction of the training costs of the
best models from the literature. We show that the Transformer generalizes well to
other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with
large and limited training data.
∗Equal contribution. Listing order is random. Jakob proposed replacing RNNs with self-attention and started
the effort to evaluate this idea. Ashish, with Illia, designed and implemented the first Transformer models and
has been crucially involved in every aspect of this work. Noam proposed scaled dot-product attention, multi-head
attention and the parameter-free position representation and became the other person involved in nearly every
detail. Niki designed, implemented, tuned and evaluated countless model variants in our original codebase and
tensor2tensor. Llion also experimented with novel model variants, was responsible for our initial codebase, and
efficient inference and visualizations. Lukasz and Aidan spent countless long days designing various parts of and
implementing tensor2tensor, replacing our earlier codebase, greatly improving results and massively accelerating
our research.
†Work performed while at Google Brain.
‡Work performed while at Google Research.
31st Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NIPS 2017), Long Beach, CA, USA.
arXiv:1706.03762v7  [cs.CL]  2 Aug 2023

1 Introduction
Recurrent neural networks, long short-term memory [13] and gated recurrent [7] neural networks
in particular, have been firmly established as state of the art approaches in sequence modeling and
transduction problems such as language modeling and machine translation [ 35, 2, 5]. Numerous
efforts have since continued to push the boundaries of recurrent language models and encoder-decoder
architectures [38, 24, 15].
Recurrent models typically factor computation along the symbol positions of the input and output
sequences. Aligning the positions to steps in computation time, they generate a sequence of hidden
states ht, as a function of the previous hidden state ht−1 and the input for position t. This inherently
sequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longer
sequence lengths, as memory constraints limit batching across examples. Recent work has achieved
significant improvements in computational efficiency through factorization tricks [21] and conditional
computation [32], while also improving model performance in case of the latter. The fundamental
constraint of sequential computation, however, remains.
Attention mechanisms have become an integral part of compelling sequence modeling and transduc-
tion models in various tasks, allowing modeling of dependencies without regard to their distance in
the input or output sequences [2, 19]. In all but a few cases [27], however, such attention mechanisms
are used in conjunction with a recurrent network.
In this work we propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and instead
relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.
The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art in
translation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.
2 Background
The goal of reducing sequential computation also forms the foundation of the Extended Neural GPU
[16], ByteNet [18] and ConvS2S [9], all of which use convolutional neural networks as basic building
block, computing hidden representations in parallel for all input and output positions. In these models,
the number of operations required to relate signals from two arbitrary input or output positions grows
in the distance between positions, linearly for ConvS2S and logarithmically for ByteNet. This makes
it more difficult to learn dependencies between distant positions [ 12]. In the Transformer this is
reduced to a constant number of operations, albeit at the cost of reduced effective resolution due
to averaging attention-weighted positions, an effect we counteract with Multi-Head Attention as
described in section 3.2.
Self-attention, sometimes called intra-attention is an attention mechanism relating different positions
of a single sequence in order to compute a representation of the sequence. Self-attention has been
used successfully in a variety of tasks including reading comprehension, abstractive summarization,
textual entailment and learning task-independent sentence representations [4, 27, 28, 22].
End-to-end memory networks are based on a recurrent attention mechanism instead of sequence-
aligned recurrence and have been shown to perform well on simple-language question answering and
language modeling tasks [34].
To the best of our knowledge, however, the Transformer is the first transduction model relying
entirely on self-attention to compute representations of its input and output without using sequence-
aligned RNNs or convolution. In the following sections, we will describe the Transformer, motivate
self-attention and discuss its advantages over models such as [17, 18] and [9].
3 Model Architecture
Most competitive neural sequence transduction models have an encoder-decoder structure [5, 2, 35].
Here, the encoder maps an input sequence of symbol representations (x1, ..., xn) to a sequence
of continuous representations z = (z1, ..., zn). Given z, the decoder then generates an output
sequence (y1, ..., ym) of symbols one element at a time. At each step the model is auto-regressive
[10], consuming the previously generated symbols as additional input when generating the next.

items.title: Winners and Losers From AI Agents | Morgan Stanley
items.summary:
The recent launch of powerful consumer AI agents has reignited debate over how artificial intelligence could disrupt industries ranging from retail and insurance to transportation and live entertainment.

Unlike traditional AI tools that primarily answer questions, these agents can browse websites, complete forms, compare prices, make purchases and even help negotiate bills. [...] By simplifying discovery, booking and transactions, AI agents could increase the use of software for such industries as transportation, local services and insurance.
   Established retailers with trusted customer relationships, competitive prices and reliable delivery networks may be better positioned to withstand disruption. [...] Local Services: An AI agent could identify an available HVAC technician, compare prices and customer reviews and book an appointment without consumers having to search for or contact multiple providers. Because local services are highly fragmented, this could generate additional business for tradespeople and benefit software platforms that connect consumers with service providers.

items.title: AI agents test and improve robot code in virtual worlds before deployment
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn't work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA's Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] "Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled," Goldberg said. "Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification."

items.title: 俺→もしすするがVRChatをテーマにした動画をつくったときの初手の挨拶を考えて
items.summary:
俺→もしすするがVRChatをテーマにした動画をつくったときの初手の挨拶を考えて
実際に動画を文字化して、全力で寄せに行って

Gemini 3.8▸ Thought for 9s
SUSURUさんが「VRChat」をテーマに動画を撮った場合の初手の挨拶と、そこから続く**動画冒頭〜最初のひとすすりまでの全力文字起こし（編集・SE・テロップ完全再現）**です。
──────
### 【初手の挨拶（決定版）】

│ 「はいどうもー！ SUSURUでーす！
│ 毎日メタバース健康生活ということで、相も変わらずVRChatにログインしているわけですけれどもー！」
│
│ (※別パターン：リアルSUSURUが初潜入する場合)
│ 「はいどうもー！ SUSURUでーす！
│ 毎日ラーメン健康生活ということで、相も変わらずラーメンをすすっているわけですけれどもー！
│ 本日はですね、なんと現実の胃袋を休めまして、メタバース！
│ VRChatの世界にうまいラーメンがあるということでやってまいりました！」
──────
### 【動画文字起こし：SUSURU TV. in VRChat】

【タイトル】
【狂気】総ポリゴン数70万超え！？メタバースの超人気ラーメンワールドですすったら、VRゴーグル越しに豚骨の匂いがしてきました。【VRChat】
──────
［0:00〜 オープニング］
(画面：あの軽快でおなじみのカントリー調フリーBGM)
(画面中央にアバター姿のSUSURU。少し首がカクカクしている)
(テロップ：黄色地に黒フチのゴシック体)

SUSURU：
「はいどうもー！ SUSURUでーす！
毎日メタバース健康生活ということで、相も変わらずVRChatにログインしているわけですけれどもー！」

(SE：ピコーン！)
(画面右上テロップ：『本日のワールド：麺屋 仮想空間 -Virtual-』)

SUSURU：
「本日はですね！
なんとフレンドのVRChatterから『SUSURUさん、メタバース空間にとんでもないクオリティの二郎系ラーメンワールドがあるから行ってくれ』とタレコミをいただきまして！
さっそくQuest 3をガッツリ被ってやってまいりました！」

(画面切り替え：ポータルに飛び込むアバターSUSURU)
(SE：シュバッ！)
──────
［0:30〜 ワールド入場・卓上チェック］
(画面：ワールドにロード完了。薄暗い雑居ビルの路地に佇むリアルなラーメン屋の店構え)

SUSURU（ナレーション）：
「さあ、インスタンスにJoinしてまいりました！
本日やってきたのは、JPチュートリアルワールドからポータルで約3秒のところにあります『麺屋 仮想空間』さんです！
Publicインスタンスということで、すでにカワイイ美少女アバターの方々がギッシリ満席！
男性アバターのSUSURU、完全に浮いておりますが、さっそく入店していきましょう！」

(SE：ガラガラ…（のれんをくぐる音）)
(画面：カウンター席に座るSUSURU)

SUSURU（ナレーション）：
「カウンターに着席しまして、まずは卓上アイテムをチェック！
おなじみのQvPenに、手鏡、そしてリセットボタンが完備！
調味料入れを掴んでみると……うおっ、ちゃんとインタラクトできて振ると『シャカシャカ』と音が鳴るギミック付き！ 製作者さんのこだわりがすでに伺えます！」
──────
［1:15〜 着丼］
(画面：厨房の奥から店主アバターが湯切りのモーション)
(BGMが一度スッと消える)
(SE：デデン！！！)
(画面がスローモーションになり、カウンターに置かれる超高精細なラーメン)

SUSURU（ナレーション）：
「そうこうしているうちにーーーーーーッ！
着丼です！！！！」

(SE：ピッカリーン！)
(画面：別アングル・ライティング・lilToonシェーダーのツヤを強調したシネマティックカメラの寄り映像)
(テロップ赤文字：『特製・全マシVR豚骨醤油ラーメン（テクスチャ4K / 30万ポリゴン）』)

SUSURU（ナレーション）：
「こちらが麺屋 仮想空間さんの、特製VR豚骨醤油ラーメンだーッ！！
うひょ〜〜〜〜〜〜〜〜ッ！！
こんもりと盛られたヤサイの上にはテラテラと輝くアブラ、そして厚さ3センチはあろうかという巨大な豚がドカンと鎮座！
lilToonのマットキャップがバチバチに効いていて、スープの湯気パーティクルからは今にも豚骨の匂いが漂ってきそう！
フレームレートが若干落ちている気もしますが、そんなことはお構いなし！
これはもう食べる前から優勝確定！」
──────
［2:00〜 実食（コール〜ファーストコンタクト）］
(画面：アバターの手でコントローラーを操作し、ラーメンのギミックを発動)
(いつもの掛け声)

SUSURU：
「それでは……すすれーーーーーーーーッ！！！（エコー）」

(SE：ズズズッ…！ ジュルルルッ…！)
(画面左下：SUSURUのワイプリアクション)

SUSURU（ナレーション）：
「まずはスープから、アバターの口元に運んで……いただきます！
ズズッ……！！」

(画面がパッと発光するエフェクト)
(SE：キラーン！)

SUSURU（ナレーション）：
「んん〜〜〜〜〜〜〜〜〜ッ！！
ンまいッッ！！！！
味は……もちろんしないわけですけれどもー！
見てくださいこのスープの質感！
ノーマルマップで緻密に表現されたアブラの膜と、コラーゲンたっぷりの乳化スープが視覚を通じて脳の満腹中枢を直接殴打してきます！
カロリーゼロなのに背徳感だけが押し寄せてくる、これぞVRの奇跡！」

(画面：ヤサイの山から箸ギミックで極太麺をリフトアップ)

SUSURU（ナレーション）：
「続いては、ウェイト設定された極太の自家製縮れ麺を……リフトして一気にすするーッ！
ズババババッ！
コシのあるポリゴン感が喉越しを刺激し、噛み締める（トリガーを引く）たびに小麦の香りがボイスチャットに乗って届きそうな勢い！
途中で卓上のお酢ギミックを回しかければ、酸味が加わってさっぱりと味変！
あまりの臨場感に、気がつけばVIVEトラッカーのバッテリー残量がゼロになるのも忘れて夢中で箸を進め……」
──────
［動画終盤：完食・エンディングへ］
(画面：空になった丼テクスチャと、お腹をさするSUSURUアバター)

SUSURU（ナレーション）：
「本日も、大変おいしくすすれました！
いやはや、満腹感はないのになぜか脳が大満足してしまう、恐るべきワールドでした！」

(画面切り替え：現実の部屋でヘッドセットを外すSUSURUの実写)

SUSURU：
「……はい！ というわけでVRChatのラーメンをすすってきたわけですけれどもー！
めちゃくちゃ完成度が高くて最高だったんですが、やっぱり普通にお腹は減ったので、これから現実の高田馬場に二郎系ラーメンを食べに行ってきまーす！
それでは、SUSURUでしたー！ また明日ー！」

(SE：カツッ！)
(画面：チャンネル登録・高評価を促すエンディング画面)
